title: Cost Ideation: Bento Views & Pricing Grammar
creator: Amaya Singh
description: Design a compact, scannable token-level cost analytics surface that combines: a) Bento card grid for fast comparison across routes/models; b) a foldable attribution rail to drill into per-invocation breakdowns; and c) an integrated visual 'pricing grammar' editor for composing and previewing pricing bands and export templates. Goal: enable PMs and infra owners to understand marginal token cost, attribute spend to model/route/segment, and compose pricing rules without leaving the console. Deliverables: Figma prototype, export schema, accessibility pass, and handoff spec for frontend + data infra.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype demonstrates Bento grid with at least three card types (summary, attribution, timeline)
Interactive pricing grammar editor supports: fixed per-token, tiered bands, and multiplier rules with live cost preview
Export produces CSV and JSON with per-invocation token-level rows and mapped attribution columns (model, route, customer_tag)
Design spec includes responsive behavior down to 960px and a condensed mobile card for 360px width
Accessibility: color contrast and keyboard nav for card expansion and grammar editor

ENG-19845 Define backend export schema and example payloads

DES-761211 Usability test with 5 internal PMs (script + recordings)

decisions: Chosen pattern: Bento grid of compact cards with left-side foldable attribution rail — balances scanability and depth
Pricing grammar will be expressed as a small DSL (human‑readable JSON under the hood) with a visual rule composer for non-technical users
Export format: default CSV with option to download JSON; include hashed customer_id column for PII safety
Adopt live preview of pricing effects on a selected date range rather than speculative forecasts to reduce confusion
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Park): 'Need clearer delineation between billable token types (prompt vs completion) — call them out visually.'
Eng (Ravi Patel): 'Backend can emit per-invocation attribution but we should limit default exports to 7 days to avoid heavy queries; provide async job for larger ranges.'
Security (Mina Ortega): 'Hashing for user_id is fine; if customers enable raw ids via enterprise contract, add audit flag and KMS requirement.'
Design Review (Sofia Chen): 'Love the bento density, but ensure the grammar editor has inline validation and undo.'

ux_tradeoffs: High-density cards improve rapid comparison but increase cognitive load — added micro affordances (sparkline + pill filters) to mitigate
Live rule preview requires immediate cost model; we limit preview sample size to representative daily slice to avoid heavy compute
Default export window is short (7 days) to protect infra; add async job for longer ranges and provide pre-signed download link
